- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) and under-estimates subsequent mean reversion; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after sharp rises.
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment divergence, model tends to over-react to recent price movements; dampen forecast sensitivity to 3–5 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often under-predicts the final 5–7 days; adjust final 5–7 days upward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to over-smooth; apply a 1–2% upward bias to avoid mean reversion trap.
- If recent history shows downward trend + positive sentiment, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 2–5% upward adjustment to forecast mid-point.
